children: must deliver 249 commercial aircraft in November and December to meet its annual goal of about 870, following 74 deliveries to 45 customers in October.
The European aircraft manufacturer reported the monthly figures on Nov. 6, bringing deliveries through October to 621. It reaffirmed its annual target during its nine-month results update on Oct. 28.
For investors, the year-end delivery pace will help determine whether Airbus
meets its financial objectives. Aircraft handovers are a key driver of revenue and cash flow, making delays significant even when customer demand remains strong.
Reaching the target would require an average of roughly 125 deliveries a month over the final two months. That would represent a sharp acceleration from October as Airbus

The final push will depend on aircraft completion and component availability across its assembly network. Investors will watch whether suppliers can support the higher pace as the company heads into 2027.

title: Airbus needs 249 year-end deliveries to meet annual target
